questions.question: What three basic questions does every economic system address?
choices: How to save, how to borrow, and when to repay loans
What to import, what to export, and when to exchange currencies
What to produce, how to produce, and for whom to produce
How to advertise, how to sell, and when to report profits

questions.question: What most strongly guides production in a traditional economy?
choices: Customs and established practices
Central production quotas alone
Stock prices alone
Competitive advertising alone

questions.question: What is a command economy?
choices: An economy with no collective production decisions
An economy with major production decisions directed by central authorities
An economy organized only by household traditions
An economy without ownership of resources

questions.question: What is a market economy?
choices: An economy where all output is assigned through inherited duties
An economy in which every price is set by one planning office
An economy with no exchange among producers
An economy relying heavily on decentralized exchange and price signals

questions.question: What is a mixed economy?
choices: An economy combining market activity with government involvement
An economy using only barter
An economy producing only imported goods
An economy with no public institutions

questions.question: What are property rights?
choices: The physical location of every factory
The total value of a country's imports
Rules concerning ownership, use, and transfer of assets
Only a firm's annual advertising expenses

questions.question: What is profit in a business context?
choices: The total amount borrowed from a bank
Revenue remaining after relevant costs are paid
The number of workers a business employs
The total value of goods before any costs

questions.question: How do market prices help coordinate decisions?
choices: They directly reveal every consumer's full preferences
They guarantee equal income for all households
They prevent any changes in production
They communicate information about relative scarcity and demand

questions.question: Why might a government provide public services in a mixed economy?
choices: Some shared needs may not be adequately met through private markets alone
Private exchange is legally impossible in mixed economies
All public services must earn the same profit as private firms
Mixed economies prohibit taxation

questions.question: What is a challenge of central planning?
choices: Avoiding any need to decide how resources are used
Ensuring every consumer has identical preferences
Collecting detailed information and adjusting decisions across a complex economy
Eliminating the need for production incentives

questions.question: Why do incentives matter in different economic systems?
choices: Incentives operate only in traditional economies
Rewards and penalties influence how people use resources
People never respond to expected benefits
Ownership makes incentives irrelevant

questions.question: How can competition affect a market economy?
choices: It requires every producer to charge an identical price
It eliminates all business failures
It prevents firms from improving products
It can encourage efficiency, innovation, and responsiveness to consumers

questions.question: Why do most modern economies not fit pure textbook models?
choices: They combine institutions, markets, regulation, and public activity
Every modern economy prohibits private trade
Textbook models describe only geography
All countries use identical ownership rules

questions.question: How does public ownership differ from private ownership?
choices: Public ownership always means no management exists
Private ownership means assets cannot be sold
Public assets are owned by government; private assets by individuals or nongovernment organizations
Public ownership applies only to household furniture

questions.question: Why is evaluating an economic system more than measuring output alone?
choices: Output has no relationship to economic activity
Distribution, choice, stability, and other outcomes also matter
Every system produces identical outcomes
Only the names of institutions determine performance

questions.question: A national planning office assigns output targets to state factories. Which model does this most resemble?
choices: Traditional household economy
Pure market economy
Subsistence barter network
Command economy

questions.question: Households exchange goods while government funds schools and regulates safety. Which description fits best?
choices: Mixed economy
Pure command economy
Pure traditional economy
Economy without public institutions

questions.question: A community allocates tasks according to inherited customary roles. Which system is most directly reflected?
choices: Pure market economy
Financial exchange market
Traditional economy
Centrally planned industrial economy

questions.question: A firm changes production after prices and consumer demand change. Which coordinating mechanism is operating?
choices: Hereditary assignment
Market signals
Military conscription
Central production quotas

questions.question: Which comparison avoids a misleading absolute claim?
choices: Market economies never have government institutions
Command economies never use any prices
Traditional economies face no resource constraints
Market and command models differ in decision-making, but actual economies may combine features
